Narrative Eligibility Justification Provide a detailed explanation of the resource’s eligibility for the National Register, including supporting historic information, methods for evaluation under the four criteria, discussion of the seven aspects of integrity, and conclusions about eligibility. For purposes of the present survey, resources within the boundary of the Area 6 Control Point Historic District were evaluated to determine if they contribute to the significance of the district. The Area 6 Control Point Historic District is currently recommended eligible for listing in the NRHP under the Secretary of the Interior’s Significance Criterion A at the national level as the location of the command center and various support facilities directly related to timing and firing operations for nuclear testing on the NNSS from 1951 to 1992. It is also eligible under Significance Criterion C for embodying the distinctive characteristics of a nuclear command center in the context of the Cold War and as a significant and distinguishable entity whose components lack individual distinction. Building 06-CP-65 contributes to the significance of the Area 6 Control Point Historic District as a warehouse facility developed to support testing and command operations at the Control Point. Regarding Criterion A, the building served as a major office and warehouse within the district. It supported REECo, a long-time contractor that provided extensive administrative support for many day-to-day site operations during the period of significance for the Control Point, as well as EG&G, which provided direct technical support to the national laboratories.
